integrity: The proof independently reconstructs the HSS error matrix. In real dimension two, the skew-symmetric Cayley factors reduce the iteration matrix to orthogonal left/right factors around the Hermitian spectral transform, giving an exact singular-value identity. The dimension-three family is explicit, keeps H=diag(1,2,4) and alpha=2 fixed, has spectral radius at most 1/3, and maps e2 to (-t/6,0,t/6), proving unbounded Euclidean transient growth.
scientific_limitations: The dimension-two contraction theorem is for real systems. The three-dimensional family fixes the Hermitian part and its condition number, rather than the spectral condition number of the full nonsymmetric matrix. The result concerns exact HSS iterations and Euclidean solution error; inexact HSS, finite precision, and the full complex 2x2 case are not classified.
title: Three dimensions are minimal for unbounded Euclidean transients in HSS
